content.prompt: Consider the curve $y=\dfrac{6}{x^3}$ for $x\ge1$. An antiderivative of $\dfrac{6}{x^3}$ is $-\dfrac{3}{x^2}$. Let $B>1$ be a finite cutoff.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area under the curve from $x=1$ to $x=B$. Give your answer in terms of $B$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The area over $[1,\infty)$ is the limit, as $B\to\infty$, of the finite areas from $x=1$ to $x=B$. As $B\to\infty$, $\dfrac{1}{B^2}\to0$. Use these facts and your answer to part a to find the area under the curve over $[1,\infty)$.

prerequisites: Integrating a power function with a given antiderivative, using the limits as [F(x)] evaluated from 1 to B (p9-review-block; p28-review-integrals)
Evaluating a definite integral with a variable upper limit (p28-review-integrals)
Area under a curve between two x-values as a definite integral (p17-definition-formula-and-graph)
Substituting into and simplifying an expression such as 3 - 3/B^2
